newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdansk shipyard sacking last 3,800 workers.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk shipyard sacking last 3,800 workers.

text.p: The bankrupt Gdansk shipyard's receiver told shocked workers on Thursday that the enterprise which gave birth to the Solidarity union would at once start laying off its last 3,800 employees.

"I have to dismiss everyone. Starting from today we are starting the process of sacking 3,800 shipyard workers," receiver Wieslaw Szaj told Reuters after delivering the grim message to employees gathered outside the main office at the yard where Lech Walesa founded Solidarity 17 years ago.

What may have been the coup de grace for the yard came on Wednesday when a second major Polish bank, Pekao SA, refused to extend a $100 million loan for construction of five ships for a German shipowner, saying terms of the prospective contract were unsatisfactory.
The receiver had hoped the loan and the German contract would have kept part of the yard alive while he and the government sought an investor to save the business.

"Let's not enter any more talks about saving the shipyard because its just a waste of time," the yard's Solidarity union chief Jerzy Borowczak told the crowd of about 1,200 stunned and angry workers, adding that they had been deceived.

The government, dominated by ex-communists, blames the yard's misfortune on its previous Solidarity-backed management and has refused to bail it out. But Solidarity, which toppled communism in Poland in 1989, says the government is denying help because of the yard's opposition links.
